lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Now I have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me analyze your situation based on the official guidance:

**For Alex (8 years old):**

According to the guidance, to qualify for Child Benefit you must:
1. Be responsible for a child under 16 (or under 20 if in approved education/training)
2. Live in the UK
3. Either live with the child OR contribute at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their upkeep

**Analysis of your circumstances:**
- ✓ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- ✓ You live in the UK
- ✓ Alex lives with you
- ✓ Alex is not in local authority care
- ✓ Alex is not in hospital or residential accommodation
- ✓ Alex is not fostered
- ✓ Alex does not work 24+ hours/week
- ✓ Alex has not started an apprenticeship in England
- ✓ Alex does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

**However, there is a critical issue:**
According to your circumstances, "Another claimant who lives with the child has priority."

The official guidance clearly states: "**Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child.**" It further explains: "If you and someone else are responsible for the same child, agree between yourselves who will get Child Benefit. If you cannot agree, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will decide who will get it."

Since another claimant who lives with Alex has priority, this means that other person would be entitled to claim Child Benefit for Alex, not you.

conversation.text:
Unfortunately, **you are not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

While Alex meets all the standard requirements (being 8 years old, living with you in the UK, not in care, etc.), the key issue is that another claimant who lives with Alex has priority to claim Child Benefit.

Under UK Child Benefit rules, **only one person can receive Child Benefit for each child**. When two people are both responsible for the same child, the rules state that you should agree between yourselves who will claim. If you cannot agree, HMRC will decide who gets it.

In your situation, since another claimant has priority, that person would be entitled to claim Child Benefit for Alex, not you. If you believe the circumstances have changed or wish to discuss this with HMRC, you should contact the Child Benefit Office directly.
